Hi Paul — thanks for the context and attachments. Short answers up front: we support a signed-jwt service-principal fallback and we can accept a daily SCIM snapshot plus intra-day PATCH deltas, with caveats around atomicity and audit logs. Details below and proposed next steps.

SAML assertion fallback options (recommended order):
- Primary: standard SAML assertion flow to PrivateCP controlplane endpoint (https://<private-cp-endpoint>/saml/acs).
- Fallback A (recommended): short-lived service principal tokens (signed JWT exchanged via our private provisioning endpoint). TTL: 15 min token, refresh via rotation every 10 min. This requires a one-time trust exchange (we'll sign a JWKS entry you host).
- Fallback B: user-bound API keys provisioned via SCIM as ephemeral credentials (least preferred — higher blast radius).

Key constraints: our fallback requires TLS mTLS between your operator host and the PrivateCP provisioning endpoint or at minimum client cert validation. We'll provide detailed cert rotation docs. For SOC/compliance, the signed-jwt flow leaves an auditable chain (issuer, kid, issuance time).

SCIM snapshot and delta model:
- Ingest model: daily full snapshot (CSV or SCIM bulk import) applied in a transactionally isolated staging window, then PATCH deltas applied for the 24h sliding window.
- Rate limits: default 500 PATCH ops/min for Private deployments; bulk snapshots are processed off-band and throttled by CPU quota. We can raise the quota for Dedicated Private customers with an SLA.
- Rollback: snapshots are recorded as ingest revisions (we retain last 7 snapshots). Rollback is a single-click revert to last snapshot plus re-apply subsequent accepted deltas; we do not automatically re-apply rejected deltas.

Audit & evidence for SOC:
- Every SCIM change (bulk or PATCH) surfaces as an audit event (user, source ip, request id).
- SAML/JWT exchanges are logged with assertion hashes, issuer, and subject.
- We can export audit logs to your syslog endpoint or push to a customer-managed S3 for retention.

Proposed immediate actions:
1) Exchange SAML metadata and a test service-principal JWKS (you attached metadata; we'll ingest a test file tomorrow).
2) We prepare a short test plan: one full snapshot import (nightly) + a sequence of PATCH deltas against the staging window.
3) 60-minute kickoff call tomorrow to walk the flow and confirm certs.

Can the team meet tomorrow at 10:30am PT? I suggest we include Jordan (operator UX), Ben (SCIM ingestion/runbook), and Tessa (security).

Thanks,
Sofia

Quick clarifications from the ingestion side:

- For bulk snapshot ingestion we expect CSV or SCIM/Bulk JSON with a manifest file (we'll validate schema v2.1). If Acme wants to push snapshots to an S3 we can pull from, we need a pre-signed URL pattern and a manifest that lists the files + checksum.
- Snapshot timing: snapshots are validated in staging, validation window is typically 10-15 minutes depending on entitlements; if validation fails we mark the snapshot as "failed" and do not apply any deltas until a new snapshot is ingested.
- Deltas (PATCH): we treat them as idempotent operations with a best-effort ordering guarantee (we tag operations with a sequence id). If you need strict linearizability for group-to-role mappings, we recommend using the service-principal exchange for those changes during the cutover period.

Attachments referenced in runbook: onboarding-snapshot-examples.md (I'll post to Drive after this thread)

Ben Carter
